The '''[[1950 in association football|1950]]–[[1951 in association football|51]] season''' was the 52nd completed season of [[The Football League]].

==Final league tables==
The tables below are reproduced here in the exact form that they can be found at [https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1950-51.html The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] website<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1950-51.html |title=England 1950-51 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24}}</ref> and in ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79'',<ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane’s, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref> with home and away statistics separated.

Beginning with the season 1894–95, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded), or more properly put, goal ratio. In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually scrapped beginning with the 1976–77 season.

From the 1922–23 season, the bottom two teams of both Third Division North and Third Division South were required to apply for [[re-election (Football League)|re-election]].<ref name=" Rothmans"/>

Newly promoted [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] won the First Division title for the first time in their history, and achieved the rare distinction of lifting the First Division title one season after promotion. They finished four points ahead of their nearest rivals [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. 

[[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] were relegated to the Second Division, bracketed together at the bottom of the First Division on 32 points. [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] survived on goal average.
